This replaces the earlier per-object reading, which rested on libmap probing MSL with the runtime profile only, whose flags lack -char signed and deferred inlining: mbstring.c, printf.c, scanf.c and string.c then placed only under GC/1.3.2. subject: TRKAppendBuffer inlining
evidence: In the target, TRKAppendBuffer (0x800DF2F8) is called out of line by TRKAppendBuffer1_ui16 (bl at 0x800DF258), TRKAppendBuffer1_ui32 (0x800DF204) and TRKAppendBuffer1_ui64 (0x800DF1A0), and TRKAppendBuffer_ui32 inlines TRKAppendBuffer1_ui32 but still calls TRKAppendBuffer (bl at 0x800DF094); TRKReadBuffer, a function of similar size, is inlined into TRKReadBuffer1_ui8 (0x800DEF9C) and the other readers. Under cflags_trk (-inline auto,deferred), src/TRK_MINNOW_DOLPHIN/msgbuf.c inlines TRKAppendBuffer into all four, which then come out at 0xC8, 0xD8, 0xFC and 0xFC bytes where the target has 0x54, 0x64, 0x88 and 0xA8. ac-decomp reaches the target with #pragma dont_inline on around TRKAppendBuffer; this project does not use per-function pragmas, so the four functions stay unmatched. No whole-file setting reproduces the target: GC/1.0 through 2.7 with -O4,p and -inline auto,deferred (1.0 to 1.2.5n keep TRKAppendBuffer1_ui32 inlined in TRKAppendBuffer_ui32, at 0xA8 bytes, but still inline TRKAppendBuffer into the three wrappers), -O2, -O3,p and -O4,s, -inline auto, on, smart, all, noauto and deferred, -inline auto,deferred with level=1, 2, 3 and 8, and -pragma "inline_max_size(n)" for n from 20 to 1000 and "inline_max_total_size(n)" for n of 100 and 10000 all either inline TRKAppendBuffer into the wrappers or stop inlining TRKReadBuffer and TRKAppendBuffer1_ui32.

subject: __shr2i
evidence: Compiler helper for long long a >> n, called from compiled code in the target (for example dolphin/pad/Pad.c). Probe: a C function performing long long a >> n, compiled with GC/1.3 and GC/1.3.2 (-nodefaults -proc gekko -align powerpc -enum int -fp hardware -O4,p), emits a bl to __shr2i instead of code, so the C operator itself cannot be its source. The target computes n - 32 once, with addic. r9,r5,-32 at 0x800E5DA8, and performs the sraw at 0x800E5DB8 before the ble at 0x800E5DBC that tests it. Under GC/1.3 and GC/1.3.2, a C rendering whose shift is unconditional (t = hi >> (n - 32); if (n - 32 > 0) lo |= t, or the same with int m = n - 32) compiles to addi with a separate compare (addic. or cmpwi), and a conditional shift (if ((m = n - 32) > 0) lo |= hi >> m) reaches a single addic. but places the sraw after the ble. Later compilers (GC/3.0a3, GC/3.0a5.2, Wii/1.0) do emit the target's opcode sequence for int m = n - 32; t = hi >> m; if (m > 0) lo |= t, so the instruction sequence alone is not decisive. What holds is the register use: the target keeps its temporaries in r8, r9 and r10 while r0, r6 and r7 stay unused, and none of the probed compilers leaves r0 unused for this code. The same r8/r9/r10 template appears in __shl2i and __shr2u, which have instruction-level markers of their own. This is the weakest of the runtime.c assembly rows: it rests on register allocation and on its family's template, not on an instruction C cannot express. Linked from the asm function in src/Runtime.PPCEABI.H/runtime.c.

subject: __AICallbackStackSwitch
evidence: Linked from an asm function in src/dolphin/ai/ai.c. The target body builds a frame, stores r1 in __OldStack, loads r1 from __CallbackStack, moves it down 8 bytes, calls the callback through mtlr / blrl, reloads r1 from __OldStack and returns through the frame. A C function cannot load r1 with another stack and come back to its own, so the original was hand-written assembly; the asm function (fralloc / frfree, as in marioparty4 5b01c79 src/dolphin/ai.c; ac-decomp writes the same frame by hand) reproduces it instruction for instruction.

subject: __AI_SRC_INIT t1 and walking
evidence: __AI_SRC_INIT declares OSTime t1 = 0, which nothing reads, and sets u32 walking (0, then 1 in the retry branch), which nothing reads. Each only holds a stack-frame slot: without t1, or without walking, the frame shrinks by 8 bytes and five instructions differ (the stwu, stmw, lmw, lwz and addi offsets). The same t1 declaration is in ac-decomp 09ca8e8 src/static/dolphin/ai/ai.c, bfbb d8e8eac src/dolphin/src/ai/ai.c, tssm fc32870 src/dolphin/src/ai/ai.c and mvp2005 f0af8a9 src/dolphin/ai/ai.c (tww 02de6b7 src/dolphin/ai/ai.c and marioparty4 5b01c79 src/dolphin/ai.c declare it the same way as unused1), and walking, under that name and in the same form, is in all six. Both are kept under the owner's 2026-10-27 write-only locals rule (CONTRIBUTING.md, Matching integrity): two or more decompilations have them in the same form, under real names. ac-decomp's other write-only locals, volume and Init_Cnt, and marioparty4's unused2, are left out because they are not load-bearing, and the rule keeps only load-bearing write-only locals: adding either one alone, initialised to 0 as ac-decomp declares it, still compiles to the target's bytes (both together grow the frame and five instructions differ). The relinked main.dol is byte-identical (SHA-1 c77fb29d39b5898933e8ef4d1ccd2ddac404554e).

subject: __GXSetVCD vertex-size tail
evidence: The upstream ac-decomp 09ca8e8 src/static/dolphin/gx/GXAttr.c has __GXSetVCD (the two VCD register writes and __GXXfVtxSpecs) and a separate __GXCalculateVLim (the vertex-size sum into gx->vLim), called from __GXSetDirtyState when gx->dirtyState has bits 0x10 or 0x8. The target has no function of that body: __GXSetVCD at 0x800FCFEC writes the registers (0x800FD00C-0x800FD02C), calls __GXXfVtxSpecs (0x800FD030), then tests gx->vNum (lhz at 0x800FD038) and, when it is not 0, adds the per-attribute sizes from the three 4-byte tables at 0x8025E630 and stores the sum to gx->vLim (sth at 0x800FD13C); __GXSetDirtyState (0x800FDF54) calls __GXSetSUTexRegs, __GXUpdateBPMask, __GXSetGenMode, __GXSetVCD and __GXSetVAT and nothing else. src/dolphin/gx/GXAttr.c writes that tail inside __GXSetVCD and src/dolphin/gx/GXGeometry.c drops the call. The normal-size factor reads gx->hasBiNrms, as the target does (lbz from offset 0x41D at 0x800FD044, then slwi by 1 at 0x800FD054 and addi 1 at 0x800FD058), where the upstream __GXCalculateVLim takes bit 9 of gx->vatA[0] and multiplies by (b == GX_NRM_NBT ? 3 : 1); the term is held in an s32 local b (b = gx->hasBiNrms; tbl3[...] * (b * 2 + 1)); with the expression written in place the compiled frame is 0x18 bytes instead of the target's 0x20. The relinked main.dol is byte-identical (SHA-1 c77fb29d39b5898933e8ef4d1ccd2ddac404554e).

subject: gTRKInterruptVectorTable
evidence: A neutral span, not a function boundary: the exception vector table from gTRKInterruptVectorTable (0x80003154) to gTRKInterruptVectorTableEnd (0x80005088), 0x1F34 bytes of .init holding the "Metrowerks Target Resident Kernel for PowerPC" string and the handlers that __TRK_reset copies over the exception vectors 0x100 bytes at a time. src/TRK_MINNOW_DOLPHIN/__exception.s assembles to these bytes and links as Matching. It is typed as one function, under the table's own label, so that objdiff counts the code; before the import it was the unnamed fn_80003154. Both edges are the table's own labels and the code on either side (TRK_memcpy ends at 0x80003154, __TRK_reset starts at 0x80005088). symbols.txt also keeps a type:label line named gTRKInterruptVectorTable at the same address: dtk's FindTRKInterruptVectorTable analysis pass adds it whenever it finds the table's header string (decomp-toolkit src/analysis/pass.rs) and writes it back on every build; it names the same address and does not affect the link.

subject: TRK_MINNOW_DOLPHIN/__exception.s
evidence: src/TRK_MINNOW_DOLPHIN/__exception.s assembles to .init of exactly 0x1F34 bytes matching this range. Animal Crossing's splits, generated from the disc's static.map, list TRK_MINNOW_DOLPHIN/__exception.s as an object of its own with comment:0, 0x1F34 bytes of .init between mem_TRK.c's .init and dolphin_trk.c's (ac-decomp 09ca8e8 config/GAFE01_00/splits.txt, 0x80003534-0x80005468); dtk's map import sets comment:0 only for an object the map names with a .s suffix. subject: gTRKInterruptVectorTable
evidence: Linked from src/TRK_MINNOW_DOLPHIN/__exception.s. The table is not a function: it is position-dependent code laid out at fixed 0x100-byte vector offsets (b __TRK_reset at +0x100, handlers at +0x200 through +0x1F00, with the 0xF00 handler branching past one at +0xF20), padded with zero words, preceded by a string, and made of instructions MWCC does not emit from C (mtsprg/mfsprg, mtsrr0/mtsrr1, rfi, mtmsr). The source writes the repeated handler bodies as two macros and places each with .org; the instructions are the target's.

subject: bink/shared/time/radcb.c volatile state and suspends
evidence: The state and suspends fields of RADCBHANDLER and RADCB are volatile in include/bink/radcb.h. The target reloads each after storing it (RADCB_resume_handler stw r9,4(r31) then lwz r0,4(r31) at 0x801208B8/0x801208BC; RADCB_resume_callback stw r9,16(r31) then lwz r0,16(r31) at 0x80120A6C/0x80120A70) and keeps RADCB_allocate_handler's state store first. subject: bink/shared/time/radcb.c bus clock read

Multiplying in the final store reloads the channel count after the *addr store and differs in 57 words; multiplying just before the *addr store differs in 38.

subject: Unlock source pointer
evidence: Unlock loads the stereo staging buffer once, before it tests the sample width (lwz r9,164(r29) at 0x80112DB4), so src/bink/src/sdk/decode/ngc/ngcsnd.c reads P->buf2 into a local beside the two task buffers. Reading P->buf2 in each call differs in 148 words.

subject: NGC_StarvedClear index
evidence: When NGC_StarvedClear finds a free task it copies the task index into the loop counter's register (mr r11,r28 at 0x80113010) and multiplies by that (mullw r0,r11,r0 at 0x8011303C), so src/bink/src/sdk/decode/ngc/ngcsnd.c sets i = idx in the found block and computes the mono buffer with i. subject: Ready task scan and stores

subject: binkread.c string.h
evidence: src/bink/src/sdk/decode/binkread.c does not include string.h and declares memmove itself. The target calls memset and memcpy the way GCC 2.95's builtins expand them. Every memcpy call is set up with crclr 4*cr1+eq, constant or variable size: checksound (0x80113BDC, 0x80113C2C, 0x80113C70), BinkOpen's track_index copy (0x80114FC8), BinkDoFrame (0x80115B1C, 0x80115B50, 0x80115B70) and BinkGetTrackData (0x801177EC). memset gets crclr only with a constant size: BinkOpen (0x80114138), BinkClose (0x80116458), BinkGetSummary (0x801167C4) and BinkOpenTrack (0x80117658); the variable-size memsets in dosilence (0x80113A38, 0x80113A48, 0x80113A5C) and BinkDoFrame's mask clear (0x80115BF4) have none. The `b` structure assignment in BinkOpen copies inline and makes no call. Prototypes compatible with the builtins (void* memset(void*, int, U32) and void* memcpy(void*, const void*, U32)) give identical bytes, as does no prototype. string.h's prototypes take size_t and conflict with the builtins; with string.h included, ProDG 3.5 changes six more functions (checksound, BinkOpen, BinkDoFrame, BinkClose, BinkGetSummary, BinkGetTrackData). memmove, which GCC 2.95 has no builtin for, is called without crclr (BinkDoFrame, 0x80115838).

subject: intelendian lwbrx
evidence: intelendian byte-swaps each word of the buffer in place with lwbrx r0,r9,r3 (0x80117A04; r9 is set to 0 before the loop at 0x80117A00) and stw. ProDG 3.5 and 3.9.3 have no C form for lwbrx: neither the shift-and-mask swap nor assembling the word from its four bytes produces it, and GCC 2.95 has no __builtin_bswap32. src/bink/src/sdk/decode/ngc/ngcfile.c writes it as one __asm__ statement with the index in an "b" operand of 0, which ProDG loads into r9 outside the loop as the target does. Approved by the project owner (Lucas, 2026-10-28) as a documented exception.

subject: ngcfile.c memmove prototype
evidence: src/bink/src/sdk/decode/ngc/ngcfile.c declares memmove itself and does not include string.h. The crclr 4*cr1+eq before the memcpy calls (0x80117AE8, 0x801181C4, 0x80118220) and the memset call (0x801183C0) comes from GCC 2.95's builtin memcpy and memset, which ProDG expands into library calls; the memmove call at 0x80117CB8 has no builtin and no crclr. Prototypes compatible with the builtins (void* memset(void*, int, U32), void* memcpy(void*, const void*, U32)) give identical bytes, as does no prototype; string.h's prototypes take size_t and conflict with the builtins.

subject: ngcfile.c volatile fields
evidence: The BinkIO counters in include/bink/binkio.h and the filepos, bufempty and cancelling fields of src/bink/src/sdk/decode/ngc/ngcfile.c's private NGCFILE area are volatile. The target reloads them after storing them and keeps their accesses in source order: BinkFileReadHeader stores filepos and reloads it (stw r0,136(r31) then lwz r11,136(r31) at 0x80117B6C/0x80117B70); CancelReadRequests stores cancelling before the cancel and after the polling loop (0x80117F88, 0x80117FAC), which the callback reads (0x80117C5C). Under ProDG 3.5, dropping volatile from error, reading, bytes_read, total_time, fg_time, buf_size, buf_peak, cur_size, cur_used, filepos, bufempty or cancelling changes at least one function; busy is decided by Bink's frame code rather than this file: BinkNextFrame stores 1 and then 0 to it with no access between (stw 0x80115DE4 and 0x80115DF0), and a non-volatile busy loses the first store. idle_time and bg_time are declared volatile like the other counters; dropping it changes no byte of this unit, and the target does not decide them yet. The other NGCFILE fields are not volatile: the target keeps their values in registers across stores.

subject: bink/src/sdk/decode/expand.c leapfrogged row pointers
evidence: ExpandPlane copies and fills 8 rows through two pointer pairs, each advanced from the other right after its row is written: d0 = d1 + pitch after the row at d0, then d1 = d0 + pitch after the row at d1. The target's type-0 copy (0x80122C6C) computes d1 and s1 first (add r7,r22,r31; add r8,r21,r31), writes row 1 through stfdx f0,r22,r31 and then alternates add rN,rM,r31 with each row, ending with mr r11,r8 and lfdux/stfdux for the last two rows. Types 2, 4, 6, 7, 8 and 9 have the same shape. Writing both updates after each pair of rows changes all of these cases. src/bink/src/sdk/decode/expand.c writes the copies through the ROWS8, ROWS8C and COPY8 macros.

subject: bink/src/sdk/decode/expand.c type 9 source reloads
evidence: ExpandPlane's raw 8x8 block (type 9) reads row k as colors.cur + 8 * k and reloads colors.cur from the BUNDLE after each store (lwz r9,104(r1) before lfd f0,24(r9) at 0x80123928/0x8012392C, and before each later row), and only then adds 64 (addi r9,r9,64). subject: bink/src/sdk/decode/expand.c motion source in one expression
evidence: The motion source of types 2, 4 and 7 is prev + pitch * (S8)*yoffs.cur++ + (S8)*xoffs.cur++, one expression. The target loads both offsets before it stores either advanced pointer (stw r11,248(r1) and stw r9,200(r1) at 0x801230FC/0x80123100, and at 0x801232AC and 0x801237A4) and multiplies pitch by the offset in that order (mullw r0,r31,r0). Two statements store yoffs.cur before loading xoffs. The source pointer is s0 itself: s0 and s1 = s0 + pitch are tested and leapfrogged without a copy.

subject: bink/src/sdk/decode/expand.c tmp byte writes
evidence: ExpandPlane's 64-byte scratch block tmp (r1+960) is written by byte through a pointer: the target addresses each byte as frame base + index + 952 (addi r0,r1,8; add r9,r0,r9; stb r6,952(r9) at 0x80122EA0-0x80122EB8, and at 0x80123D0C) and copies the block out with lfd/stfd at fixed offsets 960 to 1016(r1) (from 0x80122F44). src/bink/src/sdk/decode/expand.c declares tmp as F64 tmp[8], so the block has the 8-byte alignment its lfd/stfd copies use, and writes its bytes as ((U8*)tmp)[i]. The element type is not fixed by the target: U8 tmp[64] with the same ((U8*)tmp)[i] writes compiles to the same bytes. The pointer form of the writes is: with U8 tmp[64], plain tmp[i] subscripts make ExpandPlane 0x170C bytes (all of them) or change its code (any one of the six byte writes alone).

subject: bink/src/sdk/decode/expand.c OpenReadBundle last index
evidence: OpenReadBundle subtracts 1 from (width >> 3) * mult before adding start (addi r6,r6,-1; add r5,r5,r6 at 0x80120B70/0x80120B74) and keeps the low 16 bits with clrlwi r5,r5,16. src/bink/src/sdk/decode/expand.c computes the last index into a local and masks start + last with 0xFFFF. subject: OpenReadBundle leading-zero count
evidence: OpenReadBundle sets lenbits to 32 minus the leading zeros of the last index (cntlzw r5,r5 at 0x80120B7C, subfic r5,r5,32 at 0x80120B80). GCC 2.95 has no leading-zero builtin (__builtin_clz came with GCC 3.4) and emits cntlzw only for comparisons with zero, so src/bink/src/sdk/decode/expand.c writes the count as an __asm__ statement in its CNTLZW macro. No C form gives the bare cntlzw; subfic pair under ProDG 3.5 or 3.9.3: __builtin_clz is an external call there, __builtin_ffs computes find-first-set (neg; and; cntlzw; subfic), and a counting loop makes OpenReadBundle 25 words against the target's 22. The project owner approved inline asm for this cntlzw (2026-10-28), separately from the binkngc.c mult64anddiv and div64 uses approved on 2026-10-27, with this row as its evidence.

subject: bink/src/sdk/decode/ngc/ngcrgb.c plane pointer order
evidence: The ngcrgb.c converters take their plane pointers from S in the order u, v, y0, y1, with a0 and a1 first in the alpha converters (a0, a1, u, v, y0, y1); they read *u++, *v++, *y0++, *y1++ and then *a0++, *a1++ in the loop, and store the pointers back to S in the order u, v, y0, y1, a0, a1. ProDG schedules these accesses, so the target's instruction order is not the source order: YUV_32_4x2_even loads y1, u, v, y0 (lwz 12(r9), 16(r9), 20(r9), 8(r9) at 0x801243D8, 0x801243E0, 0x801243E8, 0x801243F0). The exact functions fix part of the order, measured by compiling the alternatives (objdiff fuzzy match): in YUV_32_4x2_even, taking y0 and y1 from S before u and v (99.69%), storing them back as y0, y1, u, v (99.54%) or u, v, y1, y0 (99.52%), or declaring v before u (99.71%) no longer matches, while reading *v++ before *u++ or declaring y1 before y0 still matches. Taking a0 and a1 last breaks YUV_32a_4x2_even (89.63%) and YUV_32am_4x2 (99.59%). Two exceptions are fixed the same way: YUV_16m_4x2 and YUV_16mx2_4x2 take y1 from S before y0 (y0 first gives 99.58% and 99.62%), and YUV_16a4m_4x2 and YUV_16a4mx2_4x2 read *a0++, *y0++, *a1++, *y1++ in the loop, the target's load order (lwz 0(r25), 0(r28), 0(r26), 0(r27) at 0x80126E60, 0x80126E64, 0x80126E70, 0x80126EAC, and 0x801270A8, 0x801270AC, 0x801270B8, 0x801270F4); reading both luma rows first gives 87.96% and 87.88% against 90.32% and 91.06%. The near misses follow the same order and are not evidence for it.

subject: bink/src/sdk/decode/ngc/ngcrgb.c r, b, g pointer order
evidence: Each pixel pair computes r = YUVTables[3][v] and b = YUVTables[0][u] before g = YUVTables[2][u] + YUVTables[1][v], and a 32-bit pixel is clamp_ytable[y][r] (clamp_ytable is a table of U32 pointers, one per luma value). YUV_32_4x2_even keeps the YUVTables rows in r15 (row 3), r16 (row 2), r17 (row 1) and r18 (row 0) (addi at 0x801243DC, 0x801243E4, 0x801243EC and 0x801243AC) and loads them in the order row 3 by v, row 1 by v, row 2 by u, row 0 by u (lwzx at 0x8012445C, 0x80124484, 0x8012448C, 0x8012449C). The target fixes only that g comes last: computing in r, g, b order leaves 20 words differing and b, g, r order 12, while b, r, g also matches. The source keeps r before b; that part is not decided by the target.

subject: bink/src/sdk/decode/ngc/ngcrgb.c grouped mono32 loads

subject: bink/src/sdk/decode/ngc/ngcrgb.c U16 luma intermediate

subject: bink/src/sdk/decode/ngc/ngcrgb.c (U16) table reads

subject: bink/src/sdk/decode/ngc/ngcrgb.c parenthesised g sum
evidence: In the 16-bit colour converters the green pointer is clamp_g + 256 + (YUVTables[2][u] + YUVTables[1][v]): the target adds the two table entries together (YUV_16_4x2_even add r6,r6,r10 at 0x80124E70) and adds the clamp_g base to the scaled sum after it (add r6,r6,r18 at 0x80124E94, r18 = clamp_g+0x400 from addi at 0x80124DDC). subject: LenBPLossless cntlzw
evidence: LenBPLossless takes the bit length of each coefficient magnitude as 32 minus its leading zeros (cntlzw r9,r9 at 0x8012D5B4, after the clrlwi r9,r9,16 of the absolute value). GCC 2.95 has no leading-zero builtin (__builtin_clz came with GCC 3.4) and emits cntlzw only for comparisons with zero, so src/bink/src/sdk/bitplane.c writes the count as an __asm__ statement in its CNTLZW macro, the same macro as expand.c and binkngc.c. Under ProDG 3.5 and 3.9.3 __builtin_clz is an external call and __builtin_ffs computes find-first-set (neg; and; cntlzw). The project owner approved inline asm for the three bitplane.c encoder uses (2026-10-28), with one row per use.

subject: LenBPLossless and encoders quad entry compare
evidence: When a quad is split, LenBPLossless, WriteBPLossless and WriteBPLossy test the length byte of the new entry against the current bit plane and only build the full entry for the store: in LenBPLossless the clrlwi r0,r11,24 and cmpw at 0x8012D8B8 compare the byte, and slwi/addi 0x300/or at 0x8012D8C4-0x8012D8CC form the entry stored with sthu. src/bink/src/sdk/bitplane.c writes the test as (U8)(*lp + ((x << 10) + 0x300)) != n and repeats the expression in the store (LENQUAD, WRITEQUAD, LOSSYWRITEQUAD). Computing the entry once into a U16 local changes the register allocation of the whole pass (98 lines of LenBPLossless differ).

subject: VARBITSPUT bit count copy
evidence: WriteBPLossless writes each coefficient magnitude with n - 1 bits (VarBitsLens is indexed by the count, for example lwz VarBitsLens+0x10 at 0x8012DD68), and the target keeps that count in a register of its own for the mask, the length update and the carry shift. src/bink/src/sdk/bitplane.c copies the count into a local (U32 _n = (n)) at the top of the VARBITSPUT macro. Using the macro argument directly changes the register allocation of WriteBPLossless (231 lines differ); WriteBPLossy compiles the same either way.

subject: WriteBPLossy refinement loop
evidence: WriteBPLossy's loop over the significant coefficients increments the index right after loading sig[i] (lbzx r0,r7,r11 at 0x8012F73C, addi r11,r11,1 at 0x8012F740), before the bit test. src/bink/src/sdk/bitplane.c writes it as i = 0; while (i < nsig) VARBITSPUT1(vb, sig[i++] & bit);. subject: game code string literals: -str reuse,readonly (no pool)

With docs/compiler_profile/game.flags changed to -str reuse,readonly, the flat/zEntShaggy.cpp table builders go from 58.58% (Shaggy0_PlayerStates), 67.62% (zEntShaggy_Anim0) and 72.36% (Shaggy0_PlayerTransitions) to 99.92%, 99.94% and 99.87%, and Shaggy0_Throw and Shaggy0_PlayerCaught from 96.43% and 95.37% to 100%, while no other function's objdiff score changes and the relinked main.dol stays byte-identical (SHA-1 c77fb29d39b5898933e8ef4d1ccd2ddac404554e); every Matching unit, zLaugh's literals included, links to the same bytes either way. subject: flat/zEntShaggy.cpp Shaggy1_ChooseThrowTarget loop locals and throw distance
evidence: Before the hangable loop Shaggy1_ChooseThrowTarget copies the frame's at.x and at.z into locals ax and az and computes the point 2.0 behind the entity into bx and bz; the loop reads only those. The target loads ent->frame and computes both behind components (two fmadds with the -2.0 constant) before mtctr at 0x80074A74-0x80074A94 and keeps all four values in f0-f3 through the loop, and SLUS-20349 (SHA-1 ebe640193e0ceb38deca343a0b576cfcba2d5920) does the same (mul.s/add.s into $f22 and $f23 with at.x/at.z in $f20/$f21 at 0x001BC5C8-0x001BC5E4, before the loop head at 0x001BC5E8). Under game.flags the compiler does not hoist these loads itself (tried with the expressions in the loop, with continue and with nested ifs: 95.99% and 95.01%). The SLUS-20349 DWARF lists no such locals (it lists two dx/dz pairs, dot, mag, timepeak, nearpt, throwdist, dropheight, hangtime, hang and i), so the four names are this project's. The throw distance is sqrtf(SQ(dx) + SQ(dz)), with SQ the inline square in include/xMathInlines.h, whose name is bfbb's (src/SB/Core/x/xMathInlines.h at d8e8eac38dd617ee72161f4cb2da4498bc89aad6, where it is only declared; credited in CREDITS.md). Each inline result is a separate value, so the target's unfused fmuls f3,f4,f4, fmuls, fadds (0x80074A00-0x80074A08) follows, where dx * dx + dz * dz compiles to an fmadds. The DWARF lists xEntGetPos (16 bytes) as an out-of-line copy from E:\SD2\Game\flat\xEnt.h, so it is an inline of that header. xVec3Sub's body is bfbb's out-of-line xVec3Sub (src/SB/Core/x/xCamera.cpp:1731; xVec3Inlines.h only declares it), made inline here; xVec3Dot is written for this project (bfbb only declares it, xVec3.h:92). Neither has a DWARF copy. The target's inlined zEntDestructObj_DestroyFX loads both model matrices first, subtracts y, x and z, and sums dy*dy first, then dx*dx and dz*dz by fmadds (0x8004AC8C-0x8004ACD4); writing the subtraction through xVec3Sub into an xVec3 local and testing xVec3Dot reproduces the register assignment, where three float locals over two xVec3 pointers do not (99.61%: they swap r3 and r5 at 0x8004AC8C-0x8004ACC0). The DWARF scope of zEntDestructObj_DestroyFX lists only rt, so the xVec3 local is not attested there; the temporary is needed for the match (the 99.61% above), and bfbb's DestroyFX has the same temporary at function scope (entDistanceFromPlayer). Declaring it in the if block or at function scope compiles the same.

subject: zEntDestructObj_Init eventFunc stores
evidence: The inlined Init stores zEntDestructObjEventCB to eventFunc (+0xC) twice: between the move and update stores (stw 0x8004B018) and again after the link pointer (lis/addi/stw 0x8004B044-0x8004B050). The source writes both stores, as bfbb d8e8eac src/SB/Game/zEntDestructObj.cpp zEntDestructObj_Init does (lines 157 and 170) and as zEntButton_Init does in this project. Dropping the first store scores zEntDestructObj_Init__FPvPv 94.27% and dropping the second 94.55% (objdiff, build/GIHE78-rev0/report.json, game.flags GC/1.3.2).

subject: zEntDestructObj_Init link pointer
evidence: The inlined Init computes link from ent->asset reloaded through the entity (lwz +0x10 at 0x8004B02C, addi 0x70 at 0x8004B030), not from the dasset local or the asset parameter it already holds in r30. The source writes (p2LinkAsset*)((zEntDestructObjAsset*)(ent->asset + 1) + 1): the links follow the 0x50-byte p2EntAsset and the 0x20-byte zEntDestructObjAsset. bfbb d8e8eac src/SB/Game/zEntDestructObj.cpp reads ent->asset too (with a raw + 0x8c for its larger asset). Taking (p2LinkAsset*)(dasset + 1) scores zEntDestructObj_Init__FPvPv 97.89% (objdiff, game.flags GC/1.3.2).

subject: zEntDestructObjEventCB (U8)~ masks
evidence: The chkby clears for events 0x54, 0x56 and 0x16 are written s->chkby &= (U8)~0x18, as bfbb d8e8eac src/SB/Game/zEntDestructObj.cpp writes them (lines 439, 451, 471) and zEntButtonEventCB does in this project; the target clears with andi. 0xE7 (0x8004ABB4, 0x8004ABE0, 0x8004AC04).
